## TL;DR
The CLI now tells users when a newer RepoOS release exists: a one-line notice on stderr for interactive commands, from a cached background check that never slows or breaks a command, with an opt-out. This round wired the documented Retry-After backoff and made the shared cache write atomic.

## Work and rationale
`update-check.ts` keeps a small cache (latest version, channel, last notice time, backoff) refreshed by a detached child, so commands never wait on the network. The notice prints at most once per 24 hours, only on a TTY, never for help/version/upgrade/serve, and honours `REPOOS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK`. Failures are cached, the cache is keyed by install channel, spawn errors and the passive hooks cannot fail a command, and a 403/429 backs off for 24 hours. Review 3 found that `Retry-After` was documented but unreachable and that the cache write could be seen truncated by a concurrent reader. `fetchLatestRelease` now throws a typed `UpdateCheckFetchError` carrying the status and the `Retry-After` delay (seconds or HTTP date), with a test, and `writeUpdateCheckCache` writes a temp file and renames it. Type check and 28 update-check tests pass.

## Approaches tried
Checking inline with a short timeout (rejected: slows commands), then a cached detached refresh with an exit-time notice, then channel keying and typed fetch errors.

## Challenges and blockers
Three review rounds on narrow edge cases of one class (shared cache races and documented-but-unwired behaviour). The engineer stalled after the Cursor outage, and the last round was finished by hand. The first handoffs failed on a missing report draft.

## Key learnings
When docs describe a behaviour, add a test that reaches it through the real code path, not a hand-built error. Write shared files atomically.
